title: Microsoft Cloud President Asks Leaders to Find 20% Cost Cuts
source_used: Stocktwits on TradingView (relays The Information) plus The Information public teaser; The Information is paywalled
key_facts: The Information reported that Microsoft has discussed cutting costs in its Azure cloud-server-rental unit by at least 20 percent, per a person with direct knowledge.
Girish Bablani, president of the Azure group that builds software for cloud servers, recently told leaders in his roughly 11,500-person division to outline cost-saving proposals.
Measures were still under consideration and could include parting with outside contractors; the report did not say categorically whether layoffs could follow.
A Microsoft spokesperson disputed the characterisation: Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans, and every responsible company prepares for a range of scenarios.

Stocktwits adds that Azure had $101.9 billion in revenue for the 12 months to June, up 40 percent, and that competitors such as Amazon Web Services and Oracle have cut staff to protect cash during AI spending.
Separately, an internal announcement on Monday by Scott Guthrie gave senior executive Arun Ulag wider oversight of key Azure units, The Information reported.
Meta and Anthropic have reportedly targeted Microsoft staff, forcing counteroffers with higher pay.
quote_evidence: Microsoft has discussed making significant cost reductions in its Azure cloud-server-rental unit, according to a person with direct knowledge of the situation.

Girish Bablani, president of the Azure group that develops software for cloud servers, recently directed leaders in his roughly 11,500-person division to outline cost-saving proposals, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
However, a Microsoft spokesperson disputed the characterization of planned cuts, saying, "Azure leadership has not directed teams to develop cost-cutting plans.
why_it_matters_hint: Even a fast-growing cloud unit is reported to be looking for savings as AI data-centre spending rises, but Microsoft denies directing cuts.
event_date: Reported 13 Oct 2026; instruction given "in recent weeks"
notes: The Information is paywalled; read Stocktwits (TradingView) relay and the public teaser. The pool headline calls Bablani "Microsoft Cloud president"; the text calls him president of Azure / of the Azure group that develops cloud-server software. The teaser says one person, the relay says people. Microsoft disputes the report, hence DISPUTED and score lowered one point.
